No. The evidence shows only a small part of the property was cleared in 2021.

- Hansen data show 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021, about 2.2% of the 3,643.5 ha asset.
- A further 37.3 ha was lost in patches under 0.5 ha. These are not counted as an event, so they are separate from the 81.3 ha.
- The event meets the corroboration rule. JRC data map 98% of the event area as forest in 2020, and later years of the series (to 2025) were observed.
- The 2021 national forest map classes 68.1 ha of the event as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). No native forest was affected, and 13.2 ha lies outside mapped forest.

The loss is therefore mostly pine plantation, which may reflect harvesting rather than conversion. These tools don't establish what happened to the land afterwards.
